limitations: Only development-case.json, parent-a/answer.txt and parent-b/answer.txt in this trial were inspected as review inputs. No confirmation case, detector result, browser, history or other input file was accessed.

Source review is against the seven explicit requirements, protected strings and supplied source record in development-case.json. The referenced RFC pages were not independently retrieved; source_review_pass does not claim fresh external source verification.

Semantic claim-unit mapping and pronoun/scope assessment are reviewer judgments. Python executed through uv verifies the exact input hashes, UTF-8 byte positions, complete boundary Cartesian product, unchanged-byte concatenation, protected-string survival, word limits and the explicit mapped claim-unit counts.

Offsets are zero-based exclusive prefix ends and suffix starts in original UTF-8 bytes. Eligible cuts consume all consecutive whitespace following a sentence-ending period, retaining existing paragraph breaks in the prefix. Neither parent contains a question mark or exclamation mark, and each has seven complete sentences; the final end-of-file boundary is excluded.

All 36 internal boundary pairs were evaluated. The five approved pairs are listed in ascending original A offset for enumeration only. No favored seam is selected or ranked; the separate deterministic chooser must apply claim-balance and offset rules.

The DTC7 fresh-reuse permission is treated as part of the full permission-and-non-guarantee claim, as required by its supplied Strength. Thus A offset 669 is invalid even though a complete-claim-only tally might hide the duplicated or omitted partial claim.
